title: Global Verdier duality at the point
statement:
Use the Poincare duality conventions of [def-pod-conventions] (so $X_0$
is smooth, separated of finite type and geometrically connected of pure
dimension $d$, not necessarily proper). The statement below also
holds verbatim for a smooth, proper, geometrically connected $k$-scheme
$X$ of pure dimension $d$ not assumed to descend to $k_0$ (see
[thm-sf-global-duality]). Let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$. For the admissible structure
morphism $a_X:X\to s$ there is a canonical isomorphism

$$
R\Gamma_c(X,K)^\vee\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(X,\mathbb D_XK),
$$

with the cohomology functors
of the fixed coefficient stage. It is natural in $K$ and compatible
with shifts. For a site-perfect
$K$, it is also compatible with finite coefficient reduction and
scalar extension under the smooth orientation and its coefficient
comparisons. At $K=\Lambda_X$ it identifies
$R\Gamma_c(X,\Lambda_X)^\vee$ with $R\Gamma(X,\omega_{X,\Lambda})$.

proof.text: Instantiate the Verdier exchange [fix-cor-verdier-exchange] at $f=a_X:X\to s$, $Y=s$, and $M=K$. The smooth separated finite-type scheme and the admissibility of $a_X$ are given by [def-pod-conventions]. The remaining structure morphism is $a_s=\operatorname{id}_s$. It satisfies [def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility]: take the identity compactification, cohomological-dimension bound $0$, identity right adjoint with identity unit and counit, and interval shifts $c^- = c^+ =0$; all coefficient comparisons are identities. Thus all three admissibility hypotheses of the exchange hold. It gives the canonical isomorphism $e_{\Lambda,K}:D_s(Ra_{X!}K)\xrightarrow{\sim}Ra_{X*}D_XK$, natural in $K$ and compatible with the specified coefficient comparisons and shifts.

Apply the functor $\operatorname{Fib}_s$ defined at all four coefficient stages in [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] to $e_{\Lambda,K}$; functors carry an isomorphism and its inverse to inverse morphisms. For $C=Ra_{X!}K$, [lem-pod-point-dualizing-complex] identifies the evaluated $D_sC$ with the derived coefficient dual of $\operatorname{Fib}_s C$. By [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], $\operatorname{Fib}_s C=R\Gamma_c(X,K)$ and $\operatorname{Fib}_s(Ra_{X*}D_XK)=R\Gamma(X,\mathbb D_XK)$. These identifications give the displayed canonical isomorphism. Their functoriality and the naturality and shift compatibility of $e$ give naturality in $K$ and shift compatibility of the result. No assertion that evaluation is an equivalence is needed for this step.

Let $K$ be site-perfect as defined in [def-weil-site-perfect-complex]. For a stipulated finite reduction or scalar extension $Q$, write $L_Q$ and $R_Q$ for the comparison maps on the source and target of the exchange $e_{\Lambda,K}$. The coefficient compatibility in the statement of [fix-cor-verdier-exchange] is the equality $R_Q\circ Q(e_{\Lambda,K})=e_{\Lambda',QK}\circ L_Q$. Apply the point functor of step 2 to this equality. The tensor, internal-Hom and evaluation identifications used to read its left side as coefficient duality respect coefficient change by [lem-fix-operation-reduction], on its stated domains: finite-quotient internal Hom uses the site-perfect first variable, integral reduction uses its derived-complete domain, and field stages use rationalization and common-stage scalar extension. That lemma also preserves the adjunction units and counits and the compact-support comparisons. For $f=a_X$ (smooth separated of pure relative dimension $d$ between separated finite-type $k$-schemes) and the unit on $s$, the smooth orientation $\eta_X=\gamma_{a_X,\Lambda}$ is compatible with every stipulated coefficient change: for $A_{E,n}\to A_{E,m}$ with $1\le m\le n$, [thm-pur-finite-reduction-of-purity] identifies the reduced orientation with the orientation at level $m$ and identifies the corresponding smooth traces; for $\mathcal O_E\to A_{E,n}$, [thm-pur-adic-reconstruction] says the integral orientation reduces exactly to $\gamma_{a_X,\Lambda_n}$ at every level $n$; for integral scalar extension $E\subset F$, the integral orientations chosen in [lem-pur-adic-purity-scalar-naturality] satisfy its comparison equation $b_{F/E}\circ C_{F/E}(\gamma_E)=\gamma_F\circ a_{F/E}$; and [thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity] says rationalization and finite extension of coefficient fields carry that adic orientation to the $E$- and $\Qlb$-orientations. Substituting these identifications in the displayed equality gives the required compatibility of the global isomorphism under the smooth orientation comparisons. In particular, this argument uses the comparison square supplied by the exchange; it does not infer a new finite-quotient ordinary-direct-image comparison isomorphism from the operation-reduction lemma.

For the unit object, [def-pod-conventions] gives $\mathbb D_X\Lambda_X=R\mathcal Hom_X(\Lambda_X,\omega_{X,\Lambda})$. The unit Hom identity is evaluation at $1$: $h\mapsto h(1)$, with inverse $x\mapsto(r\mapsto rx)$. Since internal Hom from the free rank-one unit is already the identity exact functor, its derived functor is the identity as well. Thus $\mathbb D_X\Lambda_X\cong\omega_{X,\Lambda}$, and substitution in step 2 gives $R\Gamma_c(X,\Lambda_X)^\vee\cong R\Gamma(X,\omega_{X,\Lambda})$.

For $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, steps 1--4 apply to every separated smooth $X_0$ in [def-pod-conventions]: no step replaces $Ra_{X!}$ by $Ra_{X*}$, so properness is not needed. For the alternative smooth proper geometrically connected $k$-scheme $X$ of pure dimension $d$, use the proper branch of [thm-sf-global-duality]. Its hypotheses require no descent to $k_0$ and its conclusion supplies the canonical global isomorphism, naturality, shifts, coefficient compatibilities and unit specialization. Applying $\operatorname{Fib}_s$ of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] reads its isomorphism in the point category as the displayed isomorphism of coefficient complexes. These imply the requested clauses, with coefficient compatibility restricted to site-perfect $K$; its comparisons are read under the smooth orientation of the smooth separated $a_X$ through the same orientation compatibilities as in step 3 ([thm-pur-finite-reduction-of-purity], [thm-pur-adic-reconstruction], [lem-pur-adic-purity-scalar-naturality], [thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity]), which require no descent and no properness. This appeal uses its constructible exceptional adjoint and does not assume that properness supplies the stronger ambient admissibility condition.

split_report.summary: Audited the imported theorem against the current main-20261015 blueprint and the slopmaster2 source. No new child nodes are needed: the exchange, point dualizing complex, point equivalences, ordinary/compact cohomology, site-perfect coefficient comparisons, and finite reduction of smooth purity already exist. Rewrote the proof into five cited steps, separating the exchange, point identification, site-perfect coefficient compatibility, unit specialization, and the proper non-descent case; no sorry-free declaration states the full canonical natural theorem. Second reading explicitly checks admissibility at the point, applies evaluation only as a functor, and uses the exchange comparison square without claiming extra finite-quotient ordinary-direct-image isomorphisms. The unit Hom identity is written out and statement/proof provenance is separated. Maintainer reader fix: the smooth-orientation compatibility in steps 3 and 5 now cites the orientation comparisons for integral reduction, integral scalar extension, rationalization and common-stage extension (thm-pur-adic-reconstruction, lem-pur-adic-purity-scalar-naturality, thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity), not only the finite-level square.
